assessments.title: Media and Arts | Main Contest | Visual hierarchy and composition | D4 S1
assessments.description: Week 1, day 4, slot 1: an original applied assessment in visual hierarchy and composition, situated in a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. Learners assess a practical creative decision and connect craft to audience, access, and responsible communication.
learning_objectives: Arrange clear visual hierarchy using scale and contrast.
Use grouping, alignment, balance, and space to clarify relationships.
Test work at intended size and select an evidence-based revision.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. Visual weight clusters at the left edge. What is the strongest adjustment?
options: Add or move a meaningful counterweight toward the open side
questions.correct_answer: Add or move a meaningful counterweight toward the open side
questions.rationale: Composition balance comes from the distribution of visual weight; a purposeful counterweight avoids clutter. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. How should a four-image sequence guide a clear reading path?
options: Hide the outcome in a low-contrast corner
Align frames and establish deliberate progression
questions.correct_answer: Align frames and establish deliberate progression
questions.rationale: A consistent alignment and progression help viewers follow sequence; randomness undermines it. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. How can an accent identify one priority action?
options: Reserve it for that action and keep nearby elements quieter
Apply it to every label and border
Use it only for legal copy
questions.correct_answer: Reserve it for that action and keep nearby elements quieter
questions.rationale: Limited use gives an accent a signaling role; everywhere-use makes it compete with itself. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. Aligned objects still feel chaotic. What may be missing?
questions.correct_answer: Hierarchy, grouping, and adequate spacing
questions.rationale: Alignment is only one relationship; grouping, hierarchy, and whitespace clarify what belongs together. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. Adjacent shapes fail to distinguish for low-vision users. What should be tested?
options: Luminance contrast and a distinction not dependent on hue
questions.correct_answer: Luminance contrast and a distinction not dependent on hue
questions.rationale: Luminance contrast and non-color cues can preserve distinctions across visual abilities and displays. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. A key line vanishes in a phone thumbnail. Best response?
options: Test at intended size and simplify or enlarge the essential line
questions.correct_answer: Test at intended size and simplify or enlarge the essential line
questions.rationale: Real-size testing exposes legibility problems; simplification or enlargement is more reliable than assumed zooming. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. Repeated circles link separate panels. Which principle explains their connection?
questions.correct_answer: Repetition creates recognizable rhythm
questions.rationale: Repeated forms create continuity and rhythm, though repetition by itself does not establish narrative order. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. What should a designer verify about a strong central focal point?
options: It is largest, regardless of meaning
It serves the message without obscuring essential information
questions.correct_answer: It serves the message without obscuring essential information
questions.rationale: A focal point should support the communication goal and leave necessary information accessible. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. Which change establishes a poster’s reading order?
options: Put the name behind a patterned image
Enlarge the event name and quiet secondary copy
questions.correct_answer: Enlarge the event name and quiet secondary copy
questions.rationale: Scale and weight make the primary information easy to find while preserving supporting details. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.

questions.prompt: Production case: a makerspace preparing workshop safety instructions. A caption competes with a portrait. What protects both?
options: Crop both until neither has breathing room
Keep the portrait dominant and reserve a calm caption area
Overlay text across the subject’s eyes
questions.correct_answer: Keep the portrait dominant and reserve a calm caption area
questions.rationale: A protected text area and clear hierarchy preserve the image and make its caption readable. In this setting, verify the choice against the actual audience and delivery conditions rather than assuming appearance alone is sufficient.
